songha_intro.001: Songha has claimed the front desk.
songha_intro.002: Notebook open. Pen uncapped. His watch unbuckled and laid flat beside the page, so he can read the second hand without turning his wrist.
songha_intro.003: It is the most organised anyone has ever looked behind that desk. Including you, the winter it was yours.
songha_intro.004: Don't read over my shoulder. It's not finished.
songha_intro.005: …Okay, read over my shoulder. Tell me if it's stupid.
songha_intro.006: The page is headed TONIGHT, underlined twice.
songha_intro.007: 00:50 — establish what ECHO is. 01:05 — rooms (consent first). 01:30 — food (Hamin's orders). 03:00 — ???. 04:45 — everyone near the door.
songha_intro.008: He's scheduled the haunted building. He does this. He scheduled my birthday.
songha_intro.009: And your birthday ran on time.
songha_intro.010: It ran *exactly* on time. People were scared to arrive late. Someone apologised for being early.
songha_intro.011: Everyone came. That's the point of a party.
songha_intro.012: Daniel wanders off to press something he shouldn't. Without looking up, Songha adds a line: *00:47 — Daniel, buttons. Monitor.*
songha_intro.013: "What's at three o'clock? The question marks."
songha_intro.014: That's the part I haven't solved yet. There's always a part like that.
songha_intro.015: Usually it's the part that ruins the rest.
songha_intro.016: "You've written a schedule for a night with no schedule."
songha_intro.017: That's *why* it needs one. Nobody else was going to do it.
songha_intro.018: Watch. By two a.m. every single one of them will be asking me what time it is.
songha_intro.019: Read the page properly. Every line.
songha_intro.020: He notices you reading every line. He turns the notebook a quarter-inch so it faces you better.
songha_intro.021: You worked this desk, you said. So you're my best source.
songha_intro.022: The fuse box. Where is it?
songha_intro.023: Behind Lost and Found. Under a poster of a cat.
songha_intro.024: …That's the most useful sentence anyone's said tonight.
songha_intro.025: He writes it down. *Fuse box: cat.*
songha_intro.026: Hanbi drifts past the desk and, without being asked, sets a phone charger down beside the watch.
songha_intro.028: …Twelve percent. I could see it from the sofa.
songha_intro.029: He's the only one who ever brings a charger. I've never once had to plan for it. It's unsettling.
songha_intro.030: Anyway. I think I sent something to this archive. When I was seventeen.
songha_intro.031: A plan. Five years, one page. Which means it's due. {p} This year.
songha_intro.035: Last thing. I'm doing a rota. Who stays awake, who naps on the sofa if this runs long.
songha_intro.037: "Morning. I like the part where the day hasn't done anything wrong yet."
songha_intro.038: That's a good answer. Annoyingly good. Morning. You're on the last shift, then.
songha_intro.039: "Night. It's quiet. Nobody expects anything from you at night."
songha_intro.040: …Yeah. That's fair. Night. You're with me, then. I always end up on the night shift.
songha_intro.041: "I'm a person who is awake right now. Draw your own conclusions."
songha_intro.042: That's night. I'm writing night. You don't get to be mysterious on my rota.
songha_intro.043: He writes {{playerName}} at the bottom of the list. Then he frowns, draws a neat arrow, and moves it up into the middle, as if the bottom were rude.
songha_intro.046: …Yours got a little extra. It's a long night. Don't tell Daniel.
songha_intro.048: You're here. So you're on it. That's how a rota works.
songha_intro_repeat.001: We're eleven minutes behind. I've changed "establish what ECHO is" to "establish what ECHO wants". More realistic.
songha_intro_repeat.002: Go talk to the others. You're on my rota. I know where to find you.
songha_door.001: Songha is standing in front of the door marked 03, reading the glass panel beside it like the small print on a contract.
songha_door.003: You've been through a few of these tonight. What's the success rate?
songha_door.005: That's a good metric. I'll take that metric.
songha_door.007: First: it's a piece of paper. Worst case, it's a piece of paper with bad handwriting.
songha_door.008: Second: seventeen-year-old me had strong opinions. Most of them were about me. I've survived him before.
songha_door.010: He glances at his watch. You're fairly sure he doesn't actually read it.
songha_door.011: Third, I don't have a third. I just usually have three.
songha_door.012: It's mine, and I'm saying yes. Officially. You can write that down.
songha_door.013: But you're the one standing next to the handle. So "when" is your call.
songha_door.017: That's a real answer. I'll pencil it in.
songha_door.018: He actually does. *03 — later.* He draws a small box beside the word *later*, so it can be ticked when the time comes.
songha_door.019: Honestly? Slightly relieved. I was about to come up with a fourth point.
songha_room.001: The door doesn't open onto a room. It opens onto the roof.
songha_room.002: This roof. Studio 25's own, only younger. The water tank still has all its paint. The laundromat vent breathes warm air up from four storeys below.
songha_room.003: A plastic chair with one short leg. A crate turned upside down by the tank. The air says spring before anything else does.
songha_room.005: This is two flights from the hall. ECHO built a copy of a place I could have walked to.
songha_room.006: RECORD 03 — OWNER: SONGHA. TYPE: HANDWRITTEN DOCUMENT, ONE PAGE. DATE: APRIL, FIVE YEARS AGO. 23:12. UNRESOLVED SUBJECTS: 1.
songha_room.007: The location is still available. The evening is not. That is the part I provide.
songha_room.009: "Unresolved subject." One. Somebody it can't read?
songha_room.010: I was up here alone that night. I'm fairly sure. I'd have written it down if I wasn't.
songha_room.011: He says it confidently. He says most things confidently. You are starting to learn that it isn't the same as being sure.
songha_room.013: He turns to you with the calm of a man on the last page of a mystery he solved in chapter two.
songha_room.014: It's you. I have a tally.

songha_room.021: He stops. Laughs under his breath, mostly at himself.
songha_room.022: I was about to make a plan for walking around a roof.
songha_room.024: Step one: don't fall off. Step two: see step one. That's the whole plan. It's a good plan.
songha_room.026: …Just look. Right. People do that. I've seen it done.
songha_room.027: Walk to the railing and wait for him.
songha_room.028: After a second, he follows. He stands one careful step further back from the edge than you do, and pretends it's a coincidence.
songha_room.029: The present thins out. The city below goes softer and older: a few signs that don't exist anymore, a karaoke bar that became a phone shop.
songha_room.030: On the upturned crate sits a seventeen-year-old with too much hair and a notebook balanced on one knee.
songha_room.031: His watch is off, laid flat on the crate beside him. Some habits start early.
songha_room.032: By the railing, a figure made of pale light holds a phone up to the sky.
songha_room.034: It's been loading for ten minutes.
songha_room.035: I think the sky is buffering.
songha_room.036: The boy snorts. Then looks annoyed that he snorted. He clicks his pen three times, fast.
songha_room.037: What are you even looking for?

songha_room.039: It's the same sky. That's how skies work.

songha_room.044: The light-figure lifts an arm toward a bright star low in the east, faintly orange.
songha_room.045: The reconstruction catches there, like a needle on a scratched record—
songha_room.046: —and before the figure can speak, the name is already in your mouth.
songha_room.048: Beside you, the present-day Songha turns his head. Very slowly.
songha_room.049: That one's Gerald. The app's dead, so I'm naming them myself.
songha_room.052: He can't. He looks up at it for a long moment, like a test he didn't revise for.
songha_room.055: The one that looks like it's watching you.
songha_room.056: Something small and blinking slides across the dark, left to right, steady as a metronome.
songha_room.060: The boy laughs, a loud, surprised, badly timed laugh, and claps a hand over his mouth. The building has neighbours.
songha_room.066: They're— {p} yeah, okay. They're better. They're still wrong.
songha_room.067: The light-figure's phone buzzes. Not a call. An alarm, set in advance.
songha_room.068: That's me. I have to go and lock up the front desk.
songha_room.069: You set an alarm for leaving?
songha_room.070: I always set one for leaving.
songha_room.071: The boy nods, as if that's the most sensible thing anyone has said to him all week. He's seventeen. It probably is.
songha_room.072: The real names. Will you know them by then?
songha_room.074: The stairwell door closes on the light. The boy looks at his page for a long time.
songha_room.075: Then, very neatly, he adds something in brackets.
songha_room.076: His watch lies on the crate beside him the whole time. Face up, ticking, completely ignored.
songha_room.077: How did you know it was Gerald.
songha_room.078: It isn't quite a question. He has already done the maths. He's waiting for you to show your working.
songha_room.079: "I named him. I'd know Gerald anywhere."
songha_room.080: You named a star Gerald, walked downstairs, and I never saw you again.
songha_room.081: "Because I was there. That was me."
songha_room.083: Point at the orange star, still hanging in the reconstructed east.
songha_room.084: He follows your finger up. Then back down, to you. His mouth does something complicated.
songha_room.085: I thought you were a trainee from another company. Or a ghost. I genuinely considered ghost.
songha_room.086: Every room tonight, it's been you. And I still wanted it to be you in mine. I wanted it anyway.
songha_room.087: I came back up the next three nights. Same time.
songha_room.088: He reports it like a logistics summary. Night one. Night two. Night three. Nobody.
songha_room.089: After that I figured you'd moved on. People do.

songha_room.102: I said don't say anything about the dates.

songha_room.125: …Ask me again later. I'm not strong enough yet.

songha_room.127: He looks at your hand, then at his wrist, as if working out the logistics.

songha_room.135: "We moved a lot. Leaving on time made it hurt less."
songha_room.136: I got very good at knowing when to go. The alarm meant I didn't have to decide.
songha_room.137: He doesn't answer straight away. He doesn't reach for a plan, either. He just lets it sit there, which from him is a lot.

songha_room.139: I did like you. You named a plane Minor Delay.
songha_room.140: That's not an answer, though. Try again. I'll wait. I'm practising.

songha_room.143: You don't add anything. He doesn't ask you to.

songha_room.148: See? Logged. You can't argue with a timestamp.
songha_room.149: Above you, the reconstructed sky turns a few degrees, the way it did five years ago whether anyone was watching or not.
songha_room.150: The room's going to close soon. The edges are going soft.

songha_room.154: This crate was built for one seventeen-year-old.

songha_room.163: I left before the app loaded.

songha_room.170: That makes one of us. Almost.

songha_room.172: What do I write? It's not done. It's not *not* done, either.
songha_room.174: He writes it. *In progress.* Then, smaller, underneath: *(good progress).*
songha_room.176: Asked. {p} Yeah. That's a real step. That counts.
songha_room.179: I've never left a line open on purpose in my life.
songha_room.180: He clips the pen back onto the cover without writing. It visibly costs him something. He visibly doesn't mind.

songha_room.182: Thanks for coming up. {p} Both times.
songha_hub.001: Songha is back at the front desk, notebook open to TONIGHT.

songha_route.111: ECHO doesn't build a room this time. It builds a sky.
songha_route.112: The spring sky from five years ago unfolds over the September one, faintly transparent, like tracing paper laid on a map.
songha_route.113: Two skies, a season apart, not quite lining up.
songha_route.114: Low in the east, faint and orange, is something that has no business in a September sky at four in the morning.
songha_route.117: Correction: Arcturus. It is currently below the horizon. I have restored it from the record, for reference.
songha_route.118: It returns to the pre-dawn sky every winter. Nobody schedules it.
songha_route.120: Every year. On its own. Nobody sets an alarm.
songha_route.121: The record requests real names. I hold the full catalogue. I can provide them.
songha_route.123: Sorry. No. Thank you, ECHO. {p} It says ask.
songha_route.124: He turns to you. The whole restored sky behind him, and he turns around to face the other way.
songha_route.125: You've had a whole three hours since the last time I asked. No pressure.
songha_route.126: So I'm asking. Five years late. Real names, please.
songha_route.127: You take out your phone and open the same app. Five years, three phones, and somehow it is still installed.
songha_route.131: The screen fills with thin white lines. You hold it up, and the lines settle over the stars like someone has finally labelled the shelves.
songha_route.132: That bright one, high up. Capella.
songha_route.134: The little cluster is the Pleiades. Seven sisters, supposedly. Most people can only see six.
songha_route.135: I can see six. {p} I'm going to count again later and it's going to bother me.
songha_route.136: The orange one below them is Aldebaran.
songha_route.137: Aldebaran. That's real? That sounds like one of yours.
songha_route.138: It means "the follower". It chases the Pleiades across the sky all night.
songha_route.140: Every night. It never catches up.
songha_route.141: …I don't love how much I relate to Aldebaran.
songha_route.142: He says each name carefully, twice, the way he'd run a lyric he's worried about. He doesn't write any of them down.
songha_route.143: Across the dark, something small and blinking slides left to right, steady as a metronome.
songha_route.146: Still running late, probably. Some things you don't fix.
songha_route.147: He points at one more. Faint, a little above the water tank, nothing special about it at all.
songha_route.149: Read him the real name off the screen.
songha_route.150: That's— {p} it doesn't have a name. Just a catalogue number.
songha_route.151: A number. {p} Good. I understand numbers.
songha_route.154: Kevin's real. He's real to me.
songha_route.155: He laughs, the loud, badly timed one, and this time he doesn't cover his mouth. The building is empty. There are no neighbours left to wake.
songha_route.157: He looks at it for a long time. Long enough that you start to suspect he's making a plan about it.
songha_route.160: It's when you came up the stairs. I looked. {p} Last time I'm looking tonight. Promise.

songha_route.162: His hand moves on its own. It has been moving on its own for five years.
songha_route.165: He finds the button by feel, without looking, and keeps looking at the sky. Then he unbuckles the watch and lays it face down on the concrete between you.
songha_route.166: Two skies, a season apart. A water tank, a borrowed jacket, and a watch face down on the concrete between two people who have stopped counting.
songha_route.167: For once, nobody on this roof is on their way anywhere.
songha_route.168: How long have we been up here?
songha_route.170: I don't know. {p} I genuinely don't know. I always know.
songha_route.171: It's a terrible feeling. It's a good feeling. It's mostly a good feeling.
songha_route.172: Below, the roof door opens two inches. Two cans are set on the top step with great care.
songha_route.173: Footsteps retreat: fast, then audibly slower, like someone fighting every instinct they have.
songha_route.174: Hyunjun left early. Hyunjun has never left anything early in his life.
songha_route.175: He fetches the cans and hands you one without checking the label, because he doesn't need to.
songha_route.176: Peach iced tea. You had one at midnight, by the door. Cold, even in the rain.
songha_route.177: Hot chocolate. You had one at midnight, by the door. You held it like a hand-warmer.
songha_route.178: Black coffee. You had one at midnight, by the door. At midnight. I wrote that down as a concern.
songha_route.179: Grape soda. You had one at midnight, by the door. I didn't judge. I noted.
songha_route.180: I notice inventory. It's a skill. Don't make it a thing.
songha_route.181: Can I— {p} I'm asking first. I want it on the record that I asked.
songha_route.183: Hold your hand out, palm up.
songha_route.184: He takes it the way he does everything: carefully, completely, like he'll be asked about it later.
songha_route.185: His thumb finds your knuckles and stays there, perfectly still, as if moving it would need a plan.
songha_route.187: I'll ask every time. That's the plan. Get used to it.
songha_route.188: He laces his fingers through yours. His hand is warmer than yours. You have his jacket; he has a strong sense of purpose.
songha_route.189: One more thing. Then I'll stop.
songha_route.190: He leans in, slowly enough that you could stop him at any point, and rests his forehead against yours.
songha_route.191: Just for a second. Tell me when it's been a second.
songha_route.193: Tell me when it's been two.
songha_route.194: You don't. He doesn't ask again.
songha_route.195: He leaves the cans where they are for now and sits back down beside you, closer than before.
songha_route.196: Not touching. Close enough that the jacket sleeve brushes his arm when you breathe.
songha_route.197: Is this okay? I'm asking. I want it on the record that I asked.
songha_route.199: Okay. {p} Good. I'll just be here, then. That's the whole step.
songha_route.201: He goes very still. Then, carefully, he leans back: exactly the same amount. Nothing more. It is the most precise thing he's done all night.
songha_route.202: This is nice. I'm saying that out loud so I can't pretend later I didn't notice.
songha_route.203: He picks the watch up off the concrete, still face down, and drops it into the inside pocket of the jacket you're wearing.
songha_route.204: Hold that for me. So I'm not tempted.
songha_route.207: All recipients, please come to the lobby. It is nearly time.

songha_route.210: In a minute. {p} I've got a minute. I checked. {p} I didn't check.
songha_route.211: You go down together. He holds the stairwell door, then lets it swing shut on the roof, the sky, and the laundromat vent breathing out into the dark.
songha_ending.001: In the lobby, the Archive Wall goes dark one box at a time, until a single box is left glowing, three rows up from the floor.
songha_ending.002: Record 03 selected. Owner: Songha. Writing to glass.

songha_ending.029: Below, the renovation van idles in the alley. Someone in a hard hat is eating kimbap on its bumper, in no particular hurry.
songha_ending.030: The sky over Mapo has gone from navy to grey to something softer, the colour of the inside of a shell.
songha_ending.032: Every morning for five years, this is when I'm up. For tomorrow.
songha_ending.033: Today I'm just up. Same minute. It feels completely different. I don't have data on why.
songha_ending.034: You said morning. Here it is. Delivered. Slightly early.
songha_ending.035: You said night. This is what night turns into, if you stay up for it.
songha_ending.036: Low in the southeast, one star is still hanging on while everything else fades.
songha_ending.038: Sirius. The brightest star in the sky.
songha_ending.039: The easiest one. You're starting me on the tutorial.
songha_ending.041: He takes the notebook out of his back pocket and opens the back cover. The copied page. Four dated check marks, and one line still open.
songha_ending.042: I was going to tick Year Five at sunrise. That was the plan. I had the pen out.
songha_ending.044: If I tick it, it's finished. Everything else on this page is finished.
songha_ending.045: I think I'd like one thing that isn't. Just to see what that's like.
songha_ending.046: He closes the notebook. The pen stays clipped to the cover.
songha_ending.047: His hand goes to his wrist out of habit. The watch isn't there.
songha_ending.048: It's in the inside pocket of the jacket you're still wearing. He hasn't asked for it back.
songha_ending.049: He lets his hand fall. He doesn't seem to mind.
songha_ending.053: He takes a breath, the kind that usually comes before three steps and a backup.
songha_ending.057: He says it the way he says everything, like he's already sure. This time, you think, he might be.
songha_ending.058: The building behind you is closing. The sky isn't. You stay until the last star goes, and then a little longer, because nobody has scheduled what comes after.
